statement: Stronger social relationships are associated with substantially higher survival odds — an effect the authors benchmark as comparable to smoking cessation and larger than obesity or physical inactivity.
effect_size: OR 1.50 (95% CI 1.42-1.59) increased likelihood of survival for stronger vs weaker social relationships
population: Meta-analysis of 148 prospective studies, n=308,849, mean follow-up 7.5y

provenance.primary: Holt-Lunstad, Smith & Layton - 'Social Relationships and Mortality Risk: A Meta-analytic Review', PLoS Medicine 2010
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Top-of-ladder (meta) but observational. Effect size rivals or exceeds most consumer longevity interventions in this corpus while sitting at a HIGHER evidence tier. Confounding/reverse causation (illness -> isolation) not fully excluded, but survives meta-scale adjustment. This is the domain's anchor finding.

statement: Objective social isolation, subjective loneliness, and living alone are each independently associated with increased all-cause mortality.
effect_size: Mortality OR ~1.29 (isolation), ~1.26 (loneliness), ~1.32 (living alone), all significant after adjustment

provenance.primary: Holt-Lunstad et al. - 'Loneliness and Social Isolation as Risk Factors for Mortality: A Meta-Analytic Review', Perspectives on Psychological Science 2015
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Establishes objective isolation and subjective loneliness as partly distinct risk factors. meta-tier, observational. Effect sizes are smaller than the social-relationships meta but more specifically about deficit states.

statement: When objective social isolation and subjective loneliness are modeled together, isolation predicts mortality while the loneliness association attenuates after adjustment — suggesting isolation, not loneliness per se, carries the mortality signal in this cohort.
effect_size: Isolation HR ~1.26 (fully adjusted); loneliness HR non-significant after demographic/health adjustment
population: English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA), n~6,500, age 52+

provenance.primary: Steptoe, Shankar, Demakakos & Wardle - 'Social isolation, loneliness, and all-cause mortality in older men and women', PNAS 2013
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Directly conflicts with studies foregrounding loneliness. Likely the two act via different pathways (isolation = practical/biological access; loneliness = psychological/behavioral). Open question, not resolved.

statement: Lower sense of life purpose is associated with substantially higher all-cause mortality in older US adults.
effect_size: Lowest vs highest purpose tercile: HR ~2.43 all-cause mortality over ~4y
population: Health and Retirement Study (HRS), n=6,985, age >50

provenance.primary: Alimujiang et al. - 'Association Between Life Purpose and Mortality Among US Adults Older Than 50 Years', JAMA Network Open 2019
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Large effect size, but short follow-up and observational. Purpose plausibly mediates via behavior (adherence, engagement) and stress axis; outcome is association not demonstrated lever. 'Ikigai' is the popular face of the same construct.

statement: Greater purpose in life is associated with lower all-cause mortality in community-dwelling older adults.
effect_size: High vs low purpose: HR ~0.57 mortality
population: Rush Memory and Aging Project / Minority Aging Research Study, older adults

provenance.primary: Boyle, Barnes, Buchman & Bennett - 'Purpose in Life Is Associated With Mortality Among Community-Dwelling Older Persons', Psychosomatic Medicine 2009
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Independent cohort replicating the purpose->mortality direction. Observational; healthy-personality and reverse-causation confounds.

statement: Greater purpose in life is associated with lower risk of incident Alzheimer disease and mild cognitive impairment, and slower cognitive decline.
effect_size: High vs low purpose: ~2.4x lower risk of incident AD; reduced MCI risk and slower decline
population: Rush MAP, older adults without dementia at baseline

provenance.primary: Boyle, Buchman, Barnes & Bennett - 'Effect of a Purpose in Life on Risk of Incident Alzheimer Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment in Community-Dwelling Older Persons', Archives of General Psychiatry 2010
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Cohort. Reverse causation plausible (early subclinical AD could erode sense of purpose). Cross-links Domain I (cognition) and the ikigai/Blue-Zones framing.

statement: Lower occupational/employment grade is associated with a stepwise inverse gradient in coronary heart disease mortality among British civil servants - the effect is graded across the whole hierarchy, not a poverty threshold.
effect_size: Lowest vs highest employment grade: ~3x CHD mortality; stepwise gradient at every grade
population: Whitehall I, ~18,000 male British civil servants

provenance.primary: Marmot, Rose, Shipley & Hamilton - 'Employment grade and coronary heart disease in British civil servants', Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health 1978
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: One of the most robust findings in epidemiology. The GRADIENT (not just poverty) is the key result - implicates relative position/autonomy/status, not only material deprivation. Male cohort. Partly mediated by classic risk factors but with a residual.

statement: The social gradient in mortality and morbidity replicates in a newer mixed-sex civil-servant cohort and is associated with low job control/decision latitude, pointing to psychosocial work stress as a mediator beyond classic risk factors.
effect_size: Persistent inverse social gradient; low job control associated with higher CHD risk
population: Whitehall II, ~10,000 male and female British civil servants

provenance.primary: Marmot et al. - 'Health inequalities among British civil servants: the Whitehall II study', The Lancet 1991
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Adds the job-control/autonomy mediation hypothesis. The autonomy->stress->CVD chain is plausible but the mediation claim is weaker (mechanistic) than the gradient association itself (cohort).

statement: Chronic activation of stress mediators (HPA/cortisol, sympathetic, inflammatory, metabolic) imposes a cumulative physiological cost - 'allostatic load' - proposed as the biological bridge linking psychosocial adversity (isolation, low status, low purpose) to cardiometabolic and immune aging.
effect_size: Framework; composite allostatic-load indices predict morbidity/mortality in some cohorts

provenance.primary: McEwen - 'Protective and Damaging Effects of Stress Mediators', New England Journal of Medicine 1998
provenance.surfaced_via: OpenAlex (record already archived from Domain I wave); cross-referenced

confidence_notes: Bridge HYPOTHESIS connecting the social-epi outcomes to biology. Inconsistently operationalized; risks unfalsifiability (explains more than it predicts). Tagged theoretical, NOT outcome - same discipline applied to hormesis in Domain H. Also indexed in Domain I.

statement: Frequent attendance at religious services is associated with lower all-cause mortality, mediated largely by social support, optimism, lower depression and reduced smoking - suggesting community/ritual, not metaphysics, is the active ingredient.
effect_size: Attendance >1x/week vs never: HR ~0.67 all-cause mortality over 20y
population: Nurses' Health Study, n~74,534 women, 20y follow-up

provenance.primary: Li, Stampfer, Williams & VanderWeele - 'Association of Religious Service Attendance With Mortality Among Women', JAMA Internal Medicine 2016

confidence_notes: All-female cohort; heavy healthy-adherer confounding. Sits alongside connection and purpose as another route to the same psychosocial substrate (regular community ritual). Association, not lever.

statement: By the corpus's own evidence-grading rules, the leading psychosocial mortality factors (social connection, purpose, socioeconomic position) carry larger hard-endpoint effect sizes at a HIGHER evidence tier (meta/cohort) than most supplement and device interventions (mechanistic/surrogate) - yet receive disproportionately less attention.
effect_size: Connection OR ~1.50 (meta); SES gradient ~3x; purpose HR ~2.4 (cohort) vs most supplements: surrogate-only / small

provenance.primary: Synthesis of Holt-Lunstad 2010/2015, Marmot 1978/1991, Alimujiang 2019, Boyle 2009/2010 vs the supplement/device claim tiers across Domains D/H/L

confidence_notes: A meta-observation about the FIELD's attention allocation, not a single primary study - graded by the tiers of its component claims. The honest point: these factors are under-sold because they are unmonetizable (no SKU for friendship/autonomy/meaning), which is exactly the market-driven bias an unbiased map must correct. Causation still tangled.
